p.i: A revelation given at Independence, Jackson County, Missouri, 7 August 1831, through Joseph Smith Jr.

chapter.li: LEChapter59 Verse1 Behold, blessed, says the Lord, are they who have come up unto this land with an eye single to my glory, according to my commandments, VerseEnd Verse2 for they that live shall inherit the earth, and they that die shall rest from all their labors, and their works shall follow them. And they shall receive a crown in the mansions of my Father, which I have prepared for them. VerseEnd Verse3 Yea, blessed are they whose feet stand upon the land of Zion, who have obeyed my gospel, for they shall receive for their reward the good things of the earth, and it shall bring forth in her strength. VerseEnd Verse4 And they also shall be crowned with blessings from above, yea, and with commandments not a few, and with revelations in their time, they that are faithful and diligent before me. VerseEnd

Verse5 Wherefore, I give unto them a commandment, saying thus: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your might, mind, and strength, and in the name of Jesus Christ you shall serve him. VerseEnd Verse6 You shall love your neighbor as yourself. You shall not steal, neither commit adultery, nor kill, nor do anything like unto it. VerseEnd Verse7 You shall thank the Lord your God in all things. VerseEnd Verse8 You shall offer a sacrifice unto the Lord your God in righteousness, even that of a broken heart and a contrite spirit. VerseEnd

Verse9 And that you may more fully keep yourself unspotted from the world, you shall go to the house of prayer and offer up your sacraments upon my holy day. VerseEnd Verse10 For truly, this is a day appointed unto you to rest from your labors, and to pay your devotions unto the Most High. VerseEnd Verse11 Nevertheless, your vows shall be offered up in righteousness on all days and at all times, VerseEnd Verse12 but remember that on this, the Lord’s day, you shall offer your oblations and your sacraments unto the Most High, confessing your sins unto your brethren and before the Lord. VerseEnd Verse13 And on this day, you shall do none other things — only let your food be prepared with singleness of heart, that your fasting may be perfect, or in other words, that your joy may be full. VerseEnd Verse14 Truly, this is fasting and prayer, or in other words, rejoicing and prayer. VerseEnd

Verse15 And inasmuch as you do these things with thanksgiving, with cheerful hearts and countenances (not with much laughter, for this is sin, but with a glad heart and a cheerful countenance) VerseEnd, Verse16 truly I say that inasmuch as you do this, the fullness of the earth is yours — the beasts of the fields and the fowls of the air, and that which climbs upon trees and walks upon the earth, VerseEnd Verse17 yea, and the herb, and the good things which come of the earth, whether for food, or for raiment, or for houses, or for barns, or for orchards, or for gardens, or for vineyards. VerseEnd Verse18 Yea, all things which come of the earth, in the season thereof, are made for the benefit and the use of man, both to please the eye, and to gladden the heart, VerseEnd Verse19 yea for food and for raiment, for taste and for smell, to strengthen the body and to enliven the soul. VerseEnd Verse20 And it pleases God that he has given all these things unto man, for unto this end were they made, to be used with judgment, not to excess, neither by extortion. VerseEnd

Verse21 And in nothing does man offend God, or against none is his wrath kindled, save those who confess not his hand in all things, and obey not his commandments. VerseEnd Verse22 Behold, this is according to the law and the prophets. Wherefore, trouble me no more concerning this matter, VerseEnd Verse23 but learn that he who does the works of righteousness, shall receive his reward, even peace in this world, and eternal life in the world to come. VerseEnd Verse24 I the Lord have spoken it, and the spirit bears record. Amen. VerseEnd
